text: About 500 years ago, Martin Luther wrote his 95 Theses, a list of complaints against the way the Catholic Church raised money.
Soon many people broke away from the Catholic Church and became Protestants.
src: whose use of indulgences to raise funds for Saint Peter’s Basilica was a key impetus for Martin Luther’s 95 Theses
Protestants decisively broke with the Catholic Church in the 1520s

text: The Catholic Church answered with a movement of its own, called the Counter-Reformation.
Some people in the Church had wanted change for a long time, because many priests were poorly trained.
src: The Counter-Reformation sought to renew the Catholic Church and to answer Protestantism
Calls for reform within the Catholic Church were old / Many rural priests were poorly educated and knew no Latin

text: From 1545 to 1563, church leaders met again and again at the Council of Trent.
They kept the old Catholic beliefs and set up schools to train priests better.
src: rejected all compromise with Protestants / Parish priests were to be better trained in theology through seminaries

text: New religious orders led the change, above all the Jesuits, who followed Ignatius of Loyola.
Jesuits travelled as missionaries to the Americas and Asia to spread the Catholic faith.
src: New orders led the revival, above all the Jesuits / The Jesuits, the most effective of the new orders, followed Ignatius of Loyola
they worked in rural parishes and as missionaries in the Americas and Asia

text: Catholic rulers also fought wars, and many Protestants were forced to leave their homes or change their faith.
Church leaders turned against new science too: in 1633 the scientist Galileo Galilei was kept under arrest in his house.
src: By politics, war and discriminatory law the Counter-Reformation won back Poland, Lithuania, France, Italy and the Habsburg lands, while many Protestants were expelled, forced to convert or fled
Clerical opposition also turned against new science: in 1633 Galileo Galilei was placed under house arrest

text: It changed art as well: artists like Bernini helped to create a rich new style called the Baroque.
The Counter-Reformation shaped Catholic worship for centuries.
src: The aim of restoring Catholicism’s centrality, in the Rome of Bernini and the Flanders of Rubens, was one of the drivers of the Baroque style
